s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with rash and lymphadenopathy in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
Cerebrospinal fluid with 19 white cells and normal glucose and protein concentrations
key_facts: 43-year-old man
Presented with fever, chills, and headache
Had a painless ulcer on the prepuce one month earlier
Developed fever and fatigue after the ulcer appeared
Disseminated maculopapular rash on the trunk and extremities
Multiple unprotected sexual contacts over the past three months
Diagnosed with HIV infection 10 years ago
Taking abacavir, lamivudine, darunavir, ritonavir, and dolutegravir
Undetectable viral load and a CD4 count of 1144 cells/μL
Treated with intravenous penicillin G for suspected otosyphilis one year ago
Ill-appearing but not dehydrated on examination
Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
White-cell count of 63,300/mL with a lymphomonocytic predominance
Normal blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, and urine specific gravity
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed 19 white cells with normal glucose and protein concentrations
Blood cultures were repetitively negative

shortlist.label: Secondary syphilis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of a painless ulcer on the prepuce and was previously treated for suspected otosyphilis, and now presents with a disseminated maculopapular rash and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Infectious mononucleosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which are common symptoms of infectious mononucleosis, and has a lymphomonocytic predominance on white-cell count

shortlist.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of multiple unprotected sexual contacts and presents with lymphadenopathy and a maculopapular rash, which are consistent with lymphogranuloma venereum

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to HIV infection and presents with fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which can be symptoms of toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to HIV infection and presents with fever, fatigue, and lymphadenopathy, which can be symptoms of cytomegalovirus infection

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a painless ulcer on the prepuce, followed by fever, fatigue, and a disseminated maculopapular rash, is consistent with the clinical presentation of secondary syphilis. The patient's previous diagnosis and treatment of suspected otosyphilis also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of typical symptoms such as sore throat and splenomegaly make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the typical bubo formation and proctitis associated with this condition

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not suggest toxoplasmosis, which typically presents with neurological symptoms and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid findings

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: The patient's undetectable viral load and high CD4 count make it unlikely that he would be experiencing a CMV infection
